memory: Leadership in finance is about creating a culture of excellence while maintaining humanity. At Legend Investments, I oversee a team of 180 professionals across investment, research, and operations. My leadership philosophy centers on empowerment, accountability, and continuous growth. I maintain an open-door policy, encouraging junior analysts to challenge conventional thinking. Weekly 'strategic roundtables' allow cross-level idea sharing; last month, a second-year analyst's ESG scoring approach is now portfolio-wide. Leadership is about fostering environments where innovation thrives.Talent development is prioritized through a mentorship program pairing senior managers with emerging leaders for year-long partnerships. I mentor three high-potential directors biweekly, covering deal structuring and client management. Retention rate for top performers is 94% (industry average: ~85%). Annual investments include sending 15 team members to Harvard, Stanford, and INSEAD programs. An accelerated partnership path attracts talent from Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley. Diversity initiative: 40% of senior leadership roles held by women/minorities(up from 15% since my tenure began). Partnering with SEO and Girls Who Invest to build inclusive leadership pipelines.Crisis management has shaped my leadership philosophy. During the 2020 market crash, I led the investment team on a Saturday morning during freefall, methodically analyzing positions to identify opportunities. Daily presence on the trading floor fostered trust and morale, leading to transformative hires during the downturn. Recently, managing significant redemptions in a large fund required transparent communication with investors while empowering portfolio managers. Leadership's true test lies in guiding teams through crises, not just bull markets.Innovation and adaptation drive our leadership culture. Cross-functional 'innovation pods' enable portfolio managers to collaborate with technology teams on new strategies. I chair the monthly Innovation Committee, which evaluates emerging technologies and market opportunities. Our in-house AI platform SOAR(developed by a diverse team of quants, analysts, and ML experts) exemplifies this approach. Fluid organizational structure allows talent mobility across teams, enhancing agility in evolving markets. The annual 'Future of Finance' symposium—bringing together finance, tech, and academia leaders—has generated three strategic partnerships that transformed our investment capabilities.Leadership extends beyond our firm through community engagement and social impact. I serve on three non-profit boards focused on financial literacy and economic empowerment. Our $50 million foundation initiative provides scholarships/internships for underprivileged students. I regularly speak at universities and conferences(e.g., Financial Institute National Conference) on ethical leadership. Senior executives participate in a two-week annual program teaching financial skills in underserved communities. This commitment strengthens corporate culture and attracts mission-driven talent. I believe financial success and social responsibility are mutually reinforcing, and I'm focused on developing leaders who embody both exceptional performance and unwavering integrity.Managing wealth is a discipline just like running an investment firm. While my day job is focused on institutional finance, my personal portfolio is a different game. I take a long-term approach, balancing high-risk opportunities with stable, income-generating investments. Equities and private equity make up the core, but I also hold a mix of bonds, real estate, and alternative assets. I don’t chase trends—I look for asymmetric upside. If an opportunity doesn’t have a significant margin of safety or a compelling growth narrative, it doesn’t make it into my portfolio. The goal isn’t just wealth accumulation; it’s capital preservation and strategic growth.Time management is the backbone of both my professional and personal finance strategies. My schedule is intentionally structured—mornings start at 5:30 AM with a review of global markets, followed by a workout, and then a day packed with high-stakes decision-making. I time-block everything, including personal portfolio reviews and investment research. Even weekends are structured: Saturdays are for high-level financial planning and reviewing new investment opportunities, such as an upcoming technology company, Pioneer Tech, currently engaging in pre-seed funding. Sundays are a mix of family time and catching up on reading. Having a system in place allows me to operate efficiently without missing critical financial opportunities.Investing isn’t just about numbers—it’s about vision. Looking ahead, I have clear financial goals for the next decade. On the personal side, I want to grow my private portfolio to a level where it generates substantial passive income, allowing me to step back from the day-to-day operational grind. A key strategy is expanding into AI-driven ETFs, targeting the next wave of digital investors. I also have a goal of launching a financial education initiative—building a platform that can provide free, high-quality investment education to underprivileged youth. True wealth isn’t just financial; it’s also about creating impact.Beyond the financials, personal development plays a role in how I approach wealth-building. One of my long-term goals is becoming fluent in Mandarin—China’s market influence is undeniable, and language is a gateway to understanding business culture. Another goal? Completing an Ironman triathlon before turning 50. Investing in personal resilience is just as important as investing in assets. The mental discipline required for endurance sports parallels the mindset needed in finance: strategic pacing, risk assessment, and knowing when to push forward or hold back.Ultimately, the goal is freedom—financial independence that allows for complete control over time and decision-making. In the next phase of my career, I aim to transition into a chairman role at my firm by 55, focusing more on high-level strategy and mentorship rather than the day-to-day intensity of deal-making. I also plan to establish a global investment fund with a focus on sustainable and frontier market investments, bridging the gap between profit and long-term impact. Wealth isn’t just about what you accumulate; it’s about what you build and leave behind.Networks are the foundation of influence in finance. My relationship with Sarah Chen, CEO of Pacific Dynamics, exemplifies this. We met at a Goldman conference in 2008, but our bond solidified six months later on a delayed Hong Kong flight where we bonded over market insights and jazz. This 15-year partnership transcends transactional ties—she’s now a trusted confidante I can consult at 3 AM for Asian market expertise. Such relationships are critical for strategic partnerships, crisis navigation, and staying ahead of market shifts. I actively cultivate these deep connections through intentional engagement, whether via shared interests or collaborative projects, ensuring they evolve beyond surface-level interactions.Golf is a strategic tool for relationship-building, with my memberships at National Golf Links, Cypress Point, and Muirfield serving as hubs for high-impact connections. A pivotal moment occurred during a round with Jim, CEO of MineCore, where we conceptualized a $2.3 billion merger between his company and ours. These interactions thrive on exclusivity—no phones, no interruptions—allowing organic dialogue. My 'Quarterly Links' events at Pebble Beach have become a cornerstone of client acquisition, generating three major deals and a sovereign wealth fund partnership last year. Even more valuable? My caddie, Tom, a 30-year veteran with unparalleled corporate intelligence, has provided critical insights akin to a Bloomberg terminal. Golf isn’t just a hobby; it’s a calculated strategy for fostering trust, generating deals, and accessing intelligence beyond traditional networks.Client relationships are built on personal trust, not just financial transactions. I manage 50 high-net-worth individuals and 30 institutional clients, but they receive family-office-level attention. A defining moment was helping Robert navigate his family business succession plan by spending evenings with his children, co-creating a transition strategy over family dinners. This hands-on approach extends to life events—attending weddings, supporting through personal losses, and being available at midnight for market concerns. My team calls it a 'concierge service,' but it’s about earning trust through authenticity. These relationships transcend transactions, creating loyalty that automated systems can’t replicate. This philosophy reinforces my belief that finance is ultimately about human connection, not just numbers.Travel is a cornerstone of my global network strategy, with three weekly flights between New York, London, Hong Kong, and Dubai. While exhausting, it enables face-to-face interactions that no virtual meeting can replicate. A pivotal moment was closing the Chipset Core deal in Singapore—three days of immersion, including a 4 AM dim sum run(jet lag included), transformed hesitation into a long-term partnership. I’ve adopted the '48-hour protocol' to respond to critical opportunities or clients, ensuring I can be anywhere in the world within two days. Even down to the details: my suits are tailored for long-haul flights. This relentless travel isn’t just about presence—it’s about cultural immersion, building trust through shared experiences, and understanding local contexts that shape business decisions. It’s another layer of my strategy to create relationships that transcend transactions.No work after 8 PM. Dedicated family time. Shutdown ritual. Wife’s feedback keeps me grounded. Balance is integration, not erasure. Kids’ curiosity fuels my drive. Daily choice: prioritize what matters.
